title: Boreal Retail — Inference assay for SLO Scout: latency, throughput and cost characterization
body:
Purpose:
This document records the benchmarking and performance characterization we ran for Boreal Retail's conversational product (downstream: product search assist). The goal was to answer: can Boreal meet target SLOs (p95 <= 350ms for short assistant replies, p95 <= 800ms for longer replies) at 150 qps steady with acceptable cost (target: <= $0.0009/token served) and predictable tail behavior?

Scope and constraints:
- Workload: production-ish mix provided by Boreal (70% short replies ~30–80 tokens, 30% long replies ~400–800 tokens).
- Models under test: open-variant Llama-3-70B (FP16), 8-bit quantized variant (q8), and a smaller fall-back model Llama-3-13B-int8 for graceful degradation.
- Deployment modes: Redwood Hosted (multi-tenant) and Dedicated (single-tenant reserved pool).
- Hardware targets: rwd-GPU.H100-80GB (Dedicated) and rwd-GPU.A100-80GB (Hosted baseline).
- Test window: 72-hour characterization including steady-state runs, microburst injection, and cold-cache startups.
- Measures: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side generation start to last-token emitted), tokens/sec aggregate, tokens/cost (USD/token), CPU/GPU utilization, and failure/retry rate.

Test harness and methodology:
- Harness: custom bench client (bench-suite v0.9.3) driving the Redwood API with real prompt templates and controlled concurrency. Scripts: bench-scripts/retail-mix-2029 (linked).
- Warm vs cold: each scenario run with (a) cold kernel cache and cold KV cache (server restart prior to ramp), (b) warm KV cache (100 recent prefixes), and (c) sustained-steady warm run (4 hours continuous) to measure stabilization.
- Batching: evaluated both minimal latency path (batch size=1, immediate flush) and batching window 2–10ms to allow small batching in Dedicated environment.
- Metrics collection: Prometheus for infra metrics, Redwood console logs for per-request token counts and cost attribution.

High-level results (representative numbers):
- Short replies (30–80 tokens) at 150 qps steady:
  - Hosted (A100, FP16, no batching): p50=28ms, p95=230ms, p99=420ms; tokens/sec aggregate=22k tokens/s; cost ~ $0.0011/token.
  - Dedicated (H100, FP16, batch-window=5ms): p50=24ms, p95=140ms, p99=300ms; tokens/sec aggregate=28k tokens/s; cost ~ $0.00072/token.
  - Dedicated (H100, q8): p50=22ms, p95=130ms, p99=250ms; tokens/sec=31k tokens/s; cost ~ $0.00058/token.

- Long replies (400–800 tokens) at 20 qps steady:
  - Hosted (A100, FP16): p50=520ms, p95=1.02s, p99=1.8s; tokens/sec=6.8k tokens/s; cost ~ $0.0014/token.
  - Dedicated (H100, FP16, batch-window=5ms): p50=480ms, p95=760ms, p99=1.3s; tokens/sec=9.2k tokens/s; cost ~ $0.00095/token.
  - Dedicated (H100, q8): p50=440ms, p95=690ms, p99=1.0s; tokens/sec=10.6k tokens/s; cost ~ $0.00077/token.

Tail behavior and microbursts:
- Microburst injection (500 qps for 30s): Hosted A100 showed queueing with tail >2.8s and ~2.1x request retry rate due to timeouts at the configured client timeout=3s. Dedicated H100 (reserved pool sized to 12 concurrent model instances) sustained the burst with tail p99 ~ 1.6s when batch-window increased to 8ms, otherwise p99 ~ 2.4s with batch-window=2ms. Observation: small increase to batch window during bursts significantly improved throughput at the cost of slight median increase.

Cache warmup effects:
- Cold-start: first 10 minutes after instance restart had 3–4x higher p95 for long replies due to empty KV cache and JIT kernel warmup.
- Warm-run: after warm-up tokens and prefix cache populated (approx 8k requests), p95 stabilized near the numbers above. Recommendation: implement light-weight cache pre-warm during deployment and prior to canary cutover.

Cost breakdown and sensitivity:
- Primary cost drivers: GPU occupancy time per request (dominant), inter-request batching efficiency, and token length distribution.
- Sensitivity: moving from FP16 -> q8 reduced per-token compute time by ~17% for short replies and ~21% for long replies in our runs. Pricing example: under Dedicated committed pricing, per-token cost target of $0.0009/token is achievable under q8 with batching enabled for mixed workloads at 150 qps.

Operational observations and failure modes:
- Kernel OOMs: Seen twice during aggressive microburst tests when concurrency plus dedupe caching led to temporary memory pressure on A100 instances; switched instance placement to H100 reduced OOMs.
- Retry storm: client-side aggressive retries (linear backoff 200ms) amplified tail during bursts; adding jitter and server-side rate signals reduced retry-induced load by ~40%.
- Model variance: q8 output quality drop is visible on longer context generative sections (measured by BLEU-like similarity and internal evals). Quality guardrail: route >=30% of long reply requests to FP16 or to 13B fallback for degraded quality detection.

Recommendations (high level):
1) Short term (canary-ready):
   - Deploy Dedicated H100 pool sized for expected steady qps with 15–20% burst headroom.
   - Use q8 variant for short replies by default; route long replies to FP16 until quality regressions addressed.
   - Enable a 5–8ms batching window in Dedicated to improve throughput while keeping median latency impact acceptable.
   - Implement cache pre-warm script as part of rollout pipeline (seed 5k prefixes).

2) Medium term (optimization):
   - Tune routing policy in Redwood to split requests by expected token-length (client-provided hint) and prioritize low-latency path for short replies.
   - Introduce adaptive batching: increase batch-window when queue length > threshold; revert when queue drains.
   - Add quality monitors for q8 vs FP16 contextual divergence (daily evals on representative prompt set).

3) Long term (cost & reliability):
   - Consider a hybrid: q8 for user-facing short replies; FP16 or 13B for long, high-fidelity completions; automatic fallback based on quality signals.
   - Provision a small H100 warm standby pool in an adjacent region for failover and cross-region tails.

Runbook snippets for production SLO enforcement:
- On p95 breach (short replies >350ms sustained >10min): 1) Increase batch-window by +2ms (applies to Dedicated autoscaling policy), 2) Redirect 20% short-reply traffic to 13B fallback, 3) Notify on-call SE and SRE.
- On sudden retry spike: 1) throttle ingress at edge to reduce client retries, 2) enable server token-bucket to shed non-essential requests, 3) roll forward to a canary with tightened retry backoff.

Outstanding questions for Boreal product team:
- Can we get a token-length hint from the client at request time for smarter routing?
- What is acceptable quality delta for using q8 on long replies (who owns evaluation thresholds)?
- Budget profile: is the per-token budget hard ($/token) or is there flexibility for user-facing quality improvements?

Appendix — raw numbers (selected):
- Short replies @150 qps, Dedicated H100 q8: avg per-request GPU time 18ms, p95 130ms, tokens/sec 31k, cost/token $0.00058.
- Long replies @20 qps, Dedicated H100 FP16: avg per-request GPU time 420ms, p95 760ms, tokens/sec 9.2k, cost/token $0.00095.
- Microburst 500 qps 30s: Hosted A100 p99 2.8s, Dedicated H100 p99 1.6s (batch-window=8ms).

Next steps and owner assignments:
- (Maya) prepare a condensed one-pager for Boreal execs summarizing cost vs quality tradeoffs (due 2029-11-22).
- (Diego) prototype adaptive batching policy and smoke test in staging (ETA 2029-12-02).
- (Priya) run daily quality delta evals for q8 vs FP16 on Boreal prompt set for 7 days (start 2029-11-21).

Notes and caveats:
- Results are lab-characterization under Redwood infra and the provided Boreal prompt mix; real production patterns may differ (esp. with seasonality and geo-distribution).
- Numeric cost estimates use current committed pricing; final customer pricing will be subject to contract and committed utilization assumptions.

If anything in this doc should be clarified or if Boreal wants a follow-up workshop to run A/B live traffic canary tests, flag in the linked Confluence page and tag the SE channel.
